# Results — Study 694 (Matching Low)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **two
consecutive down candles whose closes land at the same price mark a support level and the
decline reverses upward** — tested as a **long-only** event study on a fixed **30-name
liquid US large-cap + SPY** basket. For every confirming bar we enter the next open (one
lag), hold 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 trading days, and measure the forward return against the
basket's own **unconditional** base rate (not against zero — see the note below) and
against a random-draw placebo. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; 2026-07 is dropped as partial). Fingerprints `75a0fd665f4f`
(quantlab `data_stamp` on the 30-name close panel) / `a63644cb0ca5` (basket sha1,
`data.fingerprint`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` — 30 long-listed liquid US large-caps + **SPY** (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** (last complete calendar month; run 2026-07-10) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (**21.5** years; **162,180** total bars, 5,406 rows/name) |
| Fingerprints | `75a0fd665f4f` (quantlab `data_stamp`, 30-name close panel) / `a63644cb0ca5` (`data.fingerprint`, sha1 of the same closes) |
| Detector | matching low on bars (t−1, t): both **down** (`close < open`), closes matching within a **0.15%** relative tolerance (default, loose — the realistic band a scanner would accept; a strict **0.03%** tolerance and a prior-downtrend filter are tested as myth-checks) |
| Timing / costs | confirm at close of t; enter the **next open** (one lag); hold 1/5/10/20 days, **long only** (the pattern makes no short-side claim); **5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) on every event, no borrow |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names that are *still
> trading* in 2026. A fixed surviving-names panel skews slightly **toward** finding a
> working bullish-reversal signal — it excludes names whose "reversal" never came because
> they kept falling and later delisted.

## The certifying comparison — why Welch-vs-base, not a plain t-vs-zero

The basket carries the market's ordinary positive drift, so a naive one-sample *t* of the
forward return against **zero** is contaminated: a long-only event looks "significant"
merely from riding the market's up-drift, with or without any matching low. The fair test
compares the event sample against the basket's own **unconditional** forward-return pool
(what an always-long trader earns on the same names/window) via a Welch *t* — beating
"just being long the basket, any day" is the bar an actual reversal edge has to clear.
Both the plain HAC-vs-zero and the decisive Welch-vs-base numbers are reported below, and
the gap between them is the whole story.

## The headline — forward return after a matching low

| horizon | n | mean | base (unconditional) | hit-rate (Wilson 95%) | base hit-rate | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0, informational) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 4,600 | **+0.028%** | +0.028% | 52% [50.4%, 53.3%] | 51% | **−0.03** | +1.69 | 0.519 |
| 5-day  | 4,597 | **+0.245%** | +0.252% | 54% [53.0%, 55.8%] | 55% | **−0.16** | +5.49 | 0.545 |
| 10-day | 4,595 | **+0.500%** | +0.529% | 56% [55.0%, 57.9%] | 57% | **−0.48** | +7.54 | 0.646 |
| 20-day | 4,586 | **+1.051%** | +1.087% | 59% [57.5%, 60.4%] | 59% | **−0.40** | +10.55 | 0.628 |

Read it carefully: the pattern is **common** (~4,600 confirmed events on 21.5 years of a
30-name basket — a matching low fires roughly once every 24 trading days per name) and the
forward return is **positive at every horizon** — but so is the unconditional base, by
almost the *same* amount. The **decisive Welch *t*** — event sample vs the basket's own
base rate — is **never positive**, sits inside noise at every horizon (−0.03 to −0.48),
and the random-draw placebo puts every horizon at *p* ≥ 0.5 (**worse than half of random
draws in the same basket beat the observed mean**). Meanwhile the **HAC *t* vs zero**
climbs to **+10.55** by 20 days — exactly the trap the desk's methodology warns about: a
long-only signal on a basket with positive drift will *always* look "significant" against
zero, pattern or no pattern. That vs-zero number is not evidence of a matching-low
edge; it is a photograph of the market's own up-drift, and section 4a of the quants
notebook demonstrates the same trap live on a **known**-zero-edge synthetic panel.

## The long timer — cost sweep

Every event pays a fresh round trip: **5 / 10 bps one-way × 2**. Long only — no borrow.

| horizon | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +0.028% | **−0.072%** | −0.172% |
| 5-day  | +0.245% | **+0.145%** | +0.045% |
| 10-day | +0.500% | **+0.400%** | +0.300% |
| 20-day | +1.051% | **+0.951%** | +0.851% |

Nominally positive after costs from 5 days out — but that is exactly what the
unconditional base rate earns too (compare to the "base" column above, which is *not*
charged any cost in this table and still tracks the event mean almost bar for bar).
There is no *excess* here to attribute to the pattern: a trader who bought any random pair
of days in this basket, held the same horizons and paid the same costs, would have made
essentially the same money. It is the basket's own beta, not a matching-low edge.

## Bonferroni across the basket — no single name carries it either

Per-ticker Welch *t* (event sample vs that ticker's **own** unconditional pool) at the
5-day horizon, for the 30 tickers with ≥ 6 events. With **k = 30** simultaneous tests the
two-sided Bonferroni bar is **|t| ≥ 3.14** (vs the usual 1.96):

| ticker | n | mean | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| INTC | 100 | −0.492% | −2.09 |
| HD   | 149 | +0.817% | +1.84 |
| PFE  | 159 | −0.272% | −1.58 |

**0 / 30 tickers clear the corrected bar.** Even the loudest name in the basket (INTC —
and the *wrong* sign for a reversal story) doesn't survive the multiple-testing
correction. No single name is quietly carrying the pattern.

## Myth check #1 — the strict close match

Tighten the rule to a near-exact tie (closes within **0.03%** of each other, a fifth of
the default tolerance). If the lore lived in a "cleaner" match, this should surface a real
reversal edge. It doesn't (and events are roughly a quarter as common):

| horizon | n | mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 1,023 | +0.021% | −0.21 | +0.58 | 0.565 | −0.079% |
| 5-day  | 1,023 | +0.351% | +1.11 | +3.81 | 0.180 | +0.251% |
| 10-day | 1,023 | +0.568% | +0.33 | +4.84 | 0.390 | +0.468% |
| 20-day | 1,022 | +1.300% | +1.15 | +6.63 | 0.163 | +1.200% |

The strict match's Welch *t* is never negative like the loose default, but it also never
clears **+2** — the closest approach is +1.15 at 20 days. A tighter tie is not a sharper
signal; it is a smaller, still-uncertified sample.

## Myth check #2 — only matching lows after a genuine prior downtrend

A matching low is *supposed* to mark support after a real decline, not just any two red
days. Restrict to patterns whose prior trend (close two sessions before the pattern vs 10
sessions earlier) was genuinely falling — a real support test, not a random pair of down
days in a sideways or rising market:

| horizon | n | mean | Welch *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 1,784 | +0.039% | +0.37 | +1.41 | 0.383 | −0.061% |
| 5-day  | 1,783 | +0.270% | +0.23 | +3.55 | 0.416 | +0.170% |
| 10-day | 1,783 | +0.553% | +0.24 | +5.25 | 0.414 | +0.453% |
| 20-day | 1,780 | +1.278% | +1.28 | +8.25 | 0.119 | +1.178% |

Requiring a genuine prior downtrend doesn't rescue the story either — the Welch *t* stays
inside ±1.3 at every horizon. If a matching low's "support" content depended on a real
decline behind it, restricting to real declines should have sharpened the edge; it
doesn't move the needle.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic OHLCV panel (no overnight gap — the matching low needs none) with a mild
embedded drift, and a TUNABLE planted post-pattern **reversal**; no network. The
certifying statistic is Welch *t* vs the panel's own unconditional base (the same
drift-neutral comparison used on the real tape).

| world | Welch *t* (decisive) | HAC *t* (vs 0) | hit-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.13** (sd 0.93), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | — | — |
| null (edge = 0, seed 694) | +0.17 | +1.03 | 51% |
| planted edge = +0.002/day (seed 694) | **+8.32** | +9.63 | 61% |
| planted edge = +0.004/day (seed 694) | **+13.03** | +14.48 | 66% |

The null fires in 1 of 20 independent seeds at the 2-sigma bar — right at the ~5% nominal
false-positive rate of a two-sided two-sigma test, not a systematic bias — and a planted
reversal of 0.2%/day or 0.4%/day lights the detector up cleanly (*t* = 8.3 and 13.0). The
harness *would* catch a real matching-low reversal if one existed, so the real tape's
failure to certify is a genuine **absence** of signal, not a broken detector. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The certifying, drift-neutral comparison (Welch *t* vs the
  unconditional base) never certifies a reversal at any horizon (−0.03 / −0.16 / −0.48 /
  −0.40 for 1/5/10/20 days) — every reading sits inside ±0.5, nowhere near the ±2 bar. The
  random-draw placebo places every horizon at *p* ≥ 0.5 — worse than half of random picks
  in the same basket. **0 of 30 tickers** survive a Bonferroni correction individually.
  Neither the strict close-match tolerance nor a genuine prior-downtrend filter rescues
  it (best reading +1.28, still short of the bar). The **vs-zero** *t* climbs to +10.55 by
  20 days, but that is the basket's own drift, not the pattern — the gap between the two
  statistics *is* the finding. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross and net returns are nominally positive from 5 days out,
  but they track the unconditional base almost bar-for-bar — there is no *excess* return
  to charge costs against, just the basket's ordinary beta wearing a pattern's name. At
  1 day, net of even 5 bps, the trade is already negative.
- **"Marks support?" — BUSTED.** The idea that a repeated close signals a support level
  the market twice defended does not survive contact with 21.5 years of tape once
  measured fairly against what the same basket does on an ordinary day. Neither a purer
  (near-exact) match nor a genuine downtrend behind the pattern changes the verdict.
